studies.title: Self-service that absorbs the repetitive question load
studies.problem: Every organisation answers the same questions thousands of times: policies, products, order status, how-tos. It is high-volume, repetitive work spread across support, HR and IT. A human-handled contact costs a median $13.50 (Gartner), and a live chat waits about 35 seconds just for an agent's first reply (LiveChat). Knowledge workers lose about a fifth of the workday searching for information (McKinsey). Automate it once, and the saving compounds with every question asked.

flow: A multimodal front end: text, voice, or a live video avatar, on one conversational core
Retrieval-grounded answers from authoritative sources, fetched live and cited
Tiered model routing tuned for latency and cost, with automatic failover under load
Agentic actions through MCP, such as dispatching a document or a follow-up note

levers.label: Speed
levers.line: vs ~35 s for a live agent

studies.title: Touchless document processing, with people only on the exceptions
studies.problem: Invoice processing is the heartbeat of procure-to-pay, yet most AP automation is template-based OCR that breaks on a new vendor, a revised layout or a scanned copy. Every exception lands back in an AP queue, each invoice costs about $9.40 to process (Ardent Partners), and a median AP specialist handles about 12,000 invoices a year (APQC).

flow: A decision model triages the inbox, separating real documents (signal) from noise
A decision model gauges each document's complexity and picks the right-sized model to read it
Deterministic rules catch duplicates, gaps and limit breaches, then route each document to the right system
People step in only on flagged exceptions, to approve or reject

studies.title: A self-learning team of AI agents for cloud errors
studies.problem: Every cloud team hits the same cryptic errors again and again. An engineer spends 30 to 90 minutes digging through docs, Stack Overflow and GitHub issues for a fix, then the answer vanishes into a chat thread, a runbook or one person's head. About 42% of institutional knowledge is unique to the individual (Panopto), so teams keep re-triaging errors they have already solved. Generic AI tools have no memory of your confirmed fixes, and can't spot a repeat error that is worded differently.

flow: A router agent pulls the key signals from the raw error and sends it down the right path
Semantic search over the team's solved errors runs first, returning a confirmed fix at 0.85 similarity
New errors fan out to docs and community research in parallel, with fixes ranked by confidence
Each confirmed fix is embedded into a shared knowledge bank, so tacit knowledge compounds
